newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel threatens action against British Airways.
newsitem.headline: Israel threatens action against British Airways.

text.p: Israel's Civil Aviation Authority has threatened to take legal action against British Airways if the airline does not halt its new fare promotion in Israel, the head of the authority said on Wednesday.

Under the promotion, the purchaser of a British Airways ticket from London to non-European destinations such as Asia, the United States and South America, can purchase a companion ticket at half price.
This would allow Israelis to fly to third countries via London at greatly reduced fares.
"We asked them to stop immediately. If tickets are sold we will take legal steps," Menachem Sharon, director general of the Civil Aviation Authority, told Reuters.
Sharon said this was a breach of the aviation agreement between the two countries which requires Israeli approval of the British carrier's fares, even to third countries.

He said fares between Israel and the United States were already highly competitive and added that the latest promotion would hurt not only El Al, Israel's state-owned carrier, but U.S. airlines that fly to Israel, such as TWA.
Sharon noted that in the past two years two U.S. airlines -- Delta Airlines and World Airways -- have halted their flights to Tel Aviv because of the lack of profits.
A British Airways official in Tel Aviv expressed surprise at the Israeli government's reaction and said the airline "always acts in accordance with regulations."
He said the Ministry of Transportation last year issued a warning over a similar British Airways promotion but in the end did not take any action.
British Airways' promotion is the latest in a series of special deals airlines have begun offering in Israel at the start of the low season in tourism.

El Al is offering reduced fares to London as well as to Newark Airport in New Jersey via London. Air France has lowered its fare to Paris while Israel's domestic and charter carrier Arkia also has a special promotion to London.
